name: Appendix300 (laparoscopic appendectomy video + patient metadata, 5 German centres)
sources_consulted: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.09.05.25335174 (medRxiv preprint of the same descriptor; identified, not read; the Sci Data version of record was used)
trajectory_unit: One laparoscopic surgery (one patient case). Full_Videos holds the uncut, de-identified recording per case; cases with several source files are split into ordered parts (_v01, _v02, ...), counted once. Video_Snippets (100 s) and Images (<=200 frames) are derived from the same case and are not separate trajectories. Centre 1 supplied mostly 5-minute representative clips instead of full procedures.
n_trajectories_quote: The Appendix300 dataset comprises 330 laparoscopic surgery recordings, including 325 full-length laparoscopic appendectomies and 5 control recordings from non-appendectomy procedures in pediatric and adult patients treated at five German centers.

D1.quote: a timestamp, at which the appendix is fully visible prior to invasive preparation, was documented by the contributing surgery residents and fellows [...] Timestamps at which the appendix is fully visible prior to invasive preparation, the corresponding video filename (`Video` column), and laparoscopic grade (Gomes et al. scale)
D1.reason: All 330 surgeries are clinician-performed clinical cases (no programmatic collection), but no time-stamped action variable is recorded: the only temporal annotation is one event timestamp per case (appendix fully visible before dissection). No gestures, action triplets, instrument-action labels or kinematics.

D2.quote: Postoperative metadata include the histopathologic grade of appendicitis as well as the presence or absence of an appendiceal carcinoid. [...] Similarly, no data on postoperative complications are available in this dataset.
D2.reason: No outcome of the intraoperative actions is recorded; the paper states that complications are absent. The postoperative variables (histopathological grade, carcinoid) are pathologist annotations of the resected specimen. They describe the pre-existing disease state, not a consequence of an action, and there is no action variable to define "after the action". Flag for the lead: if a pathology label counted as an outcome, it is human-annotated, per case and independent of the video.

D3.quote: The “Full_Videos” directory contains one subfolder per patient (e.g., “Center1_001”), each holding the uncut, re-encoded, de-identified laparoscopic MP4 recording. [...] Center 1 provided representative 5-minute clips for the majority of cases.
D3.reason: Uncut full-procedure recordings are released for Centres 2-5 (Table 2 mean durations 29.5-33.9 min). Centre 1 (51 cases, mean 5.43 min) is mostly 5-minute clips, which would fail D3 on their own. archive_listing.txt shows a Full_Videos folder for all 330 cases.

D4.reason: Site is recorded per trajectory: the Center column of overall_merged.csv and the documented CenterX_NNN folder/file naming. Counts per CSV row (inspected): Centre1 51, Centre2 49, Centre3 42, Centre4 71, Centre5 117 (Table 1 says 118). Restricted to the continuous full-procedure centres (2-5), each still has >= 20. Device: Table 1 gives the laparoscopy system per centre only, and Centres 1 and 4 list two systems each, so device is not recorded per case. Operator: not recorded.

D5.quote: The dataset is publicly available under the Creative Commons Attribution CC-BY via the following link [...] License:** [CC BY 4.0](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
D5.reason: CC BY 4.0 (also dc.rights "Attribution 4.0 International" in the OPARA item metadata). It permits research use and release of derived material with attribution.

D6.quote: Appendix300_Full_Videos.z01 (250 GB) Appendix300_Full_Videos.z02 (250 GB) Appendix300_Full_Videos.z03 (250 GB) Appendix300_Full_Videos.z04 (250 GB) Appendix300_Full_Videos.z05 (250 GB) Appendix300_Full_Videos.zip (16.9 GB) Appendix300_Images.zip (234.11 GB) Appendix300_Video_Snippets.zip (75.23 GB)
D6.reason: Sum of the ORIGINAL bitstream sizeBytes = 1,692,471,368,687 bytes = 1.69 TB, which is <= 2.02 TB. Full videos alone are 1.36 TB (spanned zip in 6 parts).

D7.quote: each appendectomy recording was labeled with a temporal label (timestamp) marking the beginning of appendiceal dissection [...] 3,15,00:10:43.136,Center3_015.mp4
D7.reason: WEAK. The only within-video content annotation is one human-annotated timestamp per case (CSV Timestamp column). It splits each full video into two segments: before vs after full appendix visibility / start of appendiceal dissection. This is a frame/segment-level human annotation of procedural content that varies within each trajectory and is not acquisition metadata. All other labels (laparoscopic grade, perforation, histopathology, clinical data) are constant per case. If the lead requires more than a single-boundary two-segment variable, D7 = FAIL.

D8.reason: Site meets D4 and the before/after-timestamp segment variable meets D7 (weak). The cross-tab needs each full video's duration or frame count, which is not in overall_merged.csv. Container metadata could supply it. In the 100-s snippets the split is 50/50 by construction, so only full videos are informative.

counts.collection_mode: All clinician-performed clinical laparoscopic surgeries (325 appendectomies + 5 controls per paper); no programmatic collection.
counts.site: Per overall_merged.csv: Centre1 51, Centre2 49, Centre3 42, Centre4 71, Centre5 117 (= 330). Table 1: 51/49/42/71/118. Continuous full-procedure trajectories: Centres 2-5 = 279 plus an undocumented minority of Centre 1.
counts.device: Per centre only (Table 1): C1 Arthrex Synergy UHD4 / SynergyID; C2 STORZ IMAGE1 S; C3 STORZ IMAGE1 S; C4 STORZ IMAGE1 S, B. Braun AESCULAP EinsteinVision; C5 Richard Wolf ENDOCAM 4K. Not recorded per case.
counts.operator: Not recorded. Timestamps were entered by 10 named residents/fellows, but not per case.
counts.annotation_type: Per case: one timestamp (appendix fully visible before dissection); laparoscopic grade (annotation 1, 2, and 3 for 30 outliers, plus final); perforation; histopathological grade; carcinoid; preoperative clinical/laboratory data. Snippets of 100 s and up to 200 sampled frames per case.

subjects.quote: Patients with an indication of laparoscopic appendectomy for suspected acute appendicitis were included in the appendectomy dataset. [...] All included patients had a clinical indication for the surgical procedure.

notes: Candidate: passes D3, D4 (site), D5, D6, D7 (weak) and ge200, so SS-eligible pending D8. It fails RA on D1 and D2. Caveats: (i) D7 rests on a single timestamp per case; (ii) Centre 1 is mostly 5-min clips (exclude it or treat it separately for D3); (iii) overall_merged.csv flags 18 rows True in "Appendix recording from non-appendectomy laparoscopic surgery" vs 5 controls in the paper, and Centre 5 has 117 rows vs 118 in Table 1; (iv) open download without login (HTTP 200 on a HEAD request to a large bitstream; nothing large downloaded). Downloaded only readme, overall_merged.csv (82 KB), archive_listing.txt (115 KB) and licence/metadata JSON; no video.

name: Cataract-LMM (Large-scale, Multi-source, Multi-task phacoemulsification benchmark)
sources_consulted: /media/user/LaCie/medvideo_gate/DS204/hf_401/ (401 responses for subset READMEs and videos_metadata.csv)
trajectory_unit: One phacoemulsification cataract surgery (raw video RV_<ID>_S<site>.mp4). The phase / segmentation / tracking / skill subsets reuse procedures from the 3,000-video corpus (tracking and skill are capsulorhexis-phase clips of the same procedures), so they count once.
n_trajectories_quote: This resulted in a final curated dataset of 3,000 procedures, comprising 2,930 from Farabi Hospital and 70 from Noor Hospital, with a total video duration of 1,134.2 hours.

D1.quote: Temporal Phase Labels (Phase): Frame-wise annotations for 13 surgical phases across 150 videos to support automated workflow recognition. [...] The workflow commenced with an AI-based pre-annotation stage, where the Ultralytics YOLO11-L model, fine-tuned on the validated instance segmentation subset, generated initial frame-wise masks.
D1.reason: All procedures were performed by clinicians (residents, fellows, attendings). However, the only time-stamped labels are surgical phases (150 videos), which earlier batches did not count as an action variable. Instrument tracks and tips (170 capsulorhexis clips) are video-derived (AI pre-annotation plus human correction), not recorded kinematics. Both cover < 200 trajectories.

D2.quote: Quantitative Skill Assessment (Skill): Objective skill scores for 170 videos using a systematic, multi-criteria rubric, providing a foundation for standardized skill assessment. [...] The presence of critical Adverse Events was documented as a binary flag for each clip.
D2.reason: Candidate outcome: a 6-indicator skill score rated by three board-certified ophthalmic surgeons, plus an adverse-event flag (e.g. radial capsular tear), on the capsulorhexis clip of the same procedure. Human annotation, not model-derived. It covers only 170 trajectories, and the clip is the capsulorhexis phase only.

D3.quote: 3,000 complete surgical procedures encompassing 1,134.2 hours of continuous footage. [...] First, a technical quality screen was performed to exclude recordings based on pre-defined criteria: incomplete procedures, poor focus, or excessive glare obscuring key anatomical structures.
D3.reason: Full, unedited procedure recordings ("saved without post-processing"); incomplete procedures were excluded.

D4.quote: Across all subsets, the filenames for videos and extracted images (e.g., RV_0001_S1.mp4) include an S1 or S2 identifier to denote the clinical source. [...] comprising 2,930 from Farabi Hospital and 70 from Noor Hospital
D4.reason: Site, and with it device (S1 Haag-Streit HS Hi-R NEO 900; S2 ZEISS ARTEVO 800), is recorded per trajectory in the file name. The public HF tree listing (hf_tree.json) has 2,930 *_S1 and 70 *_S2 raw mp4 files, so both levels have >= 20. Phase-annotated subset: 129 S1 / 21 S2. Operator identity is not released ("protect patient and surgeon privacy").

D5.quote: released under the **[CC BY-NC-ND 4.0](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/)** [...] You **do not** have permission to use this material for commercial purposes, nor may you distribute adapted/derivative material derived from this dataset.
D5.reason: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: research use is allowed, but distributing adapted/derivative material is prohibited, so release of derived features is not permitted. Earlier batches treated NC-ND the same way (e.g. DS149).

D6.reason: HF repository storage is 814.8 GB. The current file tree (hf_tree.json) sums to 771,950,223,621 bytes, of which raw videos are 666.8 GB. Both are <= 2.02 TB.

D7.quote: annotations_full_video/: A zip archive containing individual .csv files for each source video. Each file provides temporal phase labels structured with the following columns: VideoName, phase, start_sec, end_sec, start_frame, and end_frame.
D7.reason: Human frame-wise phase labels (13 phases; three residents with expert review) vary within each of the 150 annotated full videos. There are also instance masks on 6,094 frames and tracking masks on 170 clips. Phase labels cover only 150 of 3,000 trajectories (129 S1 / 21 S2).

D8.reason: Site/device meets D4 and phase labels meet D7. The cross-tab would use the 150 phase-annotated videos (129 S1 / 21 S2); the per-video phase CSVs are gated (401) and were not inspected.

counts.collection_mode: All clinician-performed clinical surgeries (residents, fellows, expert attendings); no programmatic collection.
counts.site: S1 Farabi Eye Hospital 2,930; S2 Noor Eye Hospital 70 (file names; HF tree confirms 2,930/70 raw mp4).
counts.device: Collinear with site: Haag-Streit HS Hi-R NEO 900 (720x480, 30 fps) at S1; ZEISS ARTEVO 800 (1920x1080, 60 fps) at S2.
counts.annotation_type: Phase: 150 full videos (13 phases, frame-wise). Instance segmentation: 6,094 frames from 150 videos. Tracking: 170 capsulorhexis clips (469,118 frames, AI pre-annotation plus human verification). Skill: the same 170 clips (6 indicators, adverse-event flag, comments).

subjects.quote: A total of 3,000 phacoemulsification cataract surgery videos were prospectively collected between December 2021 and March 2025 from two ophthalmology centers in Tehran, Iran: Farabi Eye Hospital and Noor Eye Hospital. [...] Written informed consent for participation and for the use and sharing of surgical video data for research purposes was obtained from all participants at the time of data collection.

notes: Fails SS only on D5 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). Otherwise it would pass D3, D4 (site 2,930/70), D6, D7 and ge200. Fails RA on D1 and D5. HF access is gated: "This repository is publicly accessible, but you have to accept the conditions to access its files and content" (hf_page.html). Subset READMEs and videos_metadata.csv returned HTTP 401 and were not read; no conditions were accepted. Only the root README, the API JSON and the file-tree listing were saved; no video.

name: SurgBench (SurgBench-P pretraining corpus + SurgBench-E evaluation benchmark)

D5.reason: No SurgBench licence. Component licences are mixed (CC BY-NC-SA, custom, NC-ND; NC-ND sources withheld from SurgBench-E). Available only on request.

D6.reason: Only frame counts are given; no byte size.

counts.collection_mode: Mixed: clinical surgery/endoscopy, dry-lab/benchtop (JIGSAWS, AIxSuture) and VR simulation (SimSurgSkill) sources.
counts.annotation_type: 72 single-label clip classes over 6 categories (phase, camera motion, tool, disease, action, organ), inherited from source datasets.
